title: S/√B overstates the significance when S is large
caption: For B = 16 the simple S/√B and the Asimov formula agree when S ≪ B but part company as S grows. At S = 25 they give 6.25 and 5.2: the Asimov result is the one to quote when S is comparable to B, because it accounts for the Poisson spread of the background.
alt: Significance in sigma against signal counts S for background 16: a straight line S over root B and a lower curved Asimov line that separate as S grows, with 6.25 and 5.2 marked at S equal 25.
description: Simple: Z = S/√B = S/4 for B = 16, a straight line.
At S = 25 the simple formula gives 6.25σ, about 20% too high.
For small S the two curves coincide.
